narrative.overview:
MyPreflight is dispatch and cockpit tooling for people who run a virtual airline for the realism of it. The interface reads like the paperwork of a real operation — a flight plan, a loadsheet, a fuel log: exact figures, labelled units, visible subtotals, nothing decorative between the reader and the number. The document *is* the interface, and its authority comes from being correct and legible under density, not from chrome.

The system is precise, calm and document-grade. One indigo carries action and the current selection; everything else is a disciplined, faintly cool gray scale that lets tabular data — fuel in tonnes, times in `Z`, IATA and ICAO codes — be the loudest thing on the screen. Panels are flat paper on a gray canvas, separated by hairlines and tonal steps. Only things that float above the page lift off it.

It rejects the flashy gamer and sci-fi HUD: no neon, no glows, no aggressive dark-mode theatrics, no fake-cockpit skeuomorphism. Realism is earned through correct workflow and terminology, never simulated with visual gimmicks.
keyCharacteristics: Document-grade: figures are the product — exact, unit-labelled, with the derivation shown.
One signal colour: indigo means "act here" or "this is current", and nothing else.
Flat paper on canvas: hairlines and tonal steps separate surfaces; overlays alone carry shadow.
Dense but legible: built for scanning many values at once.
Dual-theme: light and dark ship together and both hold WCAG 2.1 AA.

rules.name: The Rare Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Indigo covers no more than a tenth of any screen — actions and the one current selection. If two things on a panel are indigo, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Signal-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Colour only ever means something: state, status or action. A limit breach or an emergency needs a word or an icon beside the hue, and danger red never marks anything that is not a problem — "today" on a heatmap is outlined in Ink Strong, not red.

rules.name: The Integration Brand Exception
rules.body: A third-party integration may carry its own brand hue, only on the marks that identify it — its glyph and the ring around its account avatar — never on actions, text or surfaces. **Discord** and **Discord Light** (for dark mode, since the base fails 4.5:1 on the dark canvas) are the only such tokens today. They sit within a few percent of Signal Indigo, so the integration is recognised by its logo shape, not its hue.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number a user compares or sums is set in Roboto Mono with tabular figures, right-aligned in columns, with the unit in a smaller, lighter weight. Never set comparable figures in the proportional body font.

rules.name: The Micro-Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracked labels are the system's connective tissue. The project's `tracking-wide` is 0.06em and `tracking-wider` is 0.08em; never set caps tighter than 0.06em, and never use them for reading-length text.

rules.name: The Block-Time Rule
rules.body: A flight time names its event and its certainty. Label it with the block event — Off-block, Takeoff, Arrival, On-block — and prefix "Est." or "Sched." unless it is the actual time. Before off-block a card shows off-block; after off-block it shows on-block. Add the date (`03JAN 2025`) whenever the time is not today in UTC, and never let the hyphen in "off-block" break across lines.

rules.name: The Wordmark Rule
rules.body: In prose the name is **MyPreflight**, one word, camel-cased. As a logotype beside the mark it is **mypreflight**: all lowercase, `my` at 400 and `preflight` at 700, in Signal Indigo Mark. Render it with `Wordmark` (`app/shared/ui/Wordmark.tsx`); never hand-set the logotype or bold the whole word.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Separate them with a 1px border and a tonal step, never a drop shadow. Shadow belongs only to an overlay leaving the page.

dos: Do set every comparable figure in Roboto Mono with tabular figures, unit-suffixed and column-aligned.
Do label flight times with their block event and certainty (Est. off-block, Sched. on-block), and add the date when it is not today in UTC.
Do keep Signal Indigo to one filled action per view; make the rest Alternative or Subtle.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px border and a tonal step, and keep them flat.
Do show the derivation of computed values — subtotals, running totals, build-ups.
Do pair every status colour with a word or icon, and hold 4.5:1 for text in both themes.
Do tell the user when data failed to load, and how to recover.
Do give every control a 44px target on touch screens, and keep focus rings inset inside clipped cards.
Do honour `prefers-reduced-motion`; keep state transitions around 150ms and entrances on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`.
donts: Don't build a flashy gamer or sci-fi HUD — no neon, no glows, no aggressive dark-mode theatrics, no fake-cockpit skeuomorphism.
Don't put white text on Signal Indigo Mark; fill buttons with Signal Indigo.
Don't add drop shadows to cards or panels; only modals and toasts lift.
Don't set Muted text any lighter, or use `gray-300` for anything a user must read.
Don't let a second filled indigo button compete with the primary action.
Don't show a failed request as an empty state, or a passed estimate as "now".
Don't pulse or animate anything that is not changing.
Don't reach for a modal by reflex — exhaust inline and progressive-disclosure alternatives first.
